hook: How do we know what the inside of the Earth looks like when nobody has ever been there?
about: Geophysics applies mathematics and physics to the Earth: its solid interior, oceans, atmosphere and magnetic field. Topics include earthquakes and the waves they send through the planet, the shape and gravity of the Earth, slow convection in the mantle that drives the plates, the generation of the magnetic field in the liquid core, and the circulation of air and water that makes weather and climate.

Almost nothing below the surface can be observed directly, so the area depends on inverse problems: inferring internal structure from measurements made at the surface or from satellites. The forward models come from elasticity and fluid dynamics on a rotating sphere. Data are noisy and incomplete, and the governing equations are often chaotic, so statistics, numerical simulation and data assimilation are central.

example.title: How far away was the earthquake?
example.text: An earthquake sends out fast P waves and slower S waves. Suppose they travel at 6 km/s and 3.5 km/s, and a station records the S wave 30 seconds after the P wave. The distance \(d\) satisfies \(d/3.5 - d/6 = 30\), so \(d = 252\) km. One station gives only a circle of possible locations. Circles from three stations meet in a single point, the epicenter.

theorems.name: Clairaut's theorem
theorems.statement: For a slowly rotating body in hydrostatic equilibrium, gravity at latitude \(\varphi\) is, to first order, \(g = g_e\left[1 + \left(\frac52 m - f\right)\sin^2\varphi\right]\), where \(f\) is the flattening and \(m\) the ratio of centrifugal acceleration to gravity at the equator.

theorems.name: Speeds of elastic waves
theorems.statement: An isotropic elastic solid with Lamé constants \(\lambda\), \(\mu\) and density \(\rho\) carries compressional waves at speed \(\sqrt{(\lambda + 2\mu)/\rho}\) and shear waves at speed \(\sqrt{\mu/\rho}\). Shear waves do not propagate in a fluid, where \(\mu = 0\).

theorems.name: Herglotz-Wiechert inversion
theorems.statement: In a spherically symmetric Earth where \(r/v(r)\) decreases steadily with depth, the travel times of waves between surface points determine the wave speed \(v(r)\) uniquely, through an explicit formula of Abel type.

theorems.name: Geostrophic balance
theorems.statement: For large-scale, slowly changing flow away from the equator, the Coriolis force balances the horizontal pressure gradient: \(f\,\hat z\times u = -\nabla_h p/\rho\), with \(f = 2\Omega\sin\varphi\). The wind therefore blows along lines of constant pressure.

theorems.name: Cowling's theorem
theorems.statement: A magnetic field that is symmetric about an axis cannot be maintained by dynamo action.

theorems.name: Gutenberg-Richter law
theorems.statement: In a given region and time span, the number \(N\) of earthquakes of magnitude at least \(M\) follows \(\log_{10}N = a - bM\), with \(b\) close to 1. This is an empirical law.

open.name: Earthquake prediction
open.gloss: Can the time, place and size of individual large earthquakes be forecast with useful accuracy?

open.name: Reversals of the magnetic field
open.gloss: Explain and simulate, at realistic parameter values, why the geodynamo reverses polarity at irregular intervals.

open.name: Limits of climate prediction
open.gloss: How precisely can the response of the climate system to a given forcing be determined?
